reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the formation of borides, enhanced grain boundary cohesion, and improved ductility/work hardenability in the specific HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy. However, it provides no evidence regarding performance under irradiation or high-temperature exposure, leaving the key premise about stability under those conditions unsupported.
premises: Boron addition (0.1 at.%) to an equimolar HfMoNbTaTiZr RHEA induces HCP boride precipitates at grain boundaries.
These boride precipitates enhance grain boundary cohesion.
Enhanced grain boundary cohesion improves ductility and work hardenability.
The matrix remains a BCC solid solution with unchanged hardness.
The proposed mechanism and outcome will hold under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
